import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 63

Let $A$ be the smallest set containing $2$ and $3$ and such that $a_1a_2 - 1 \in A$
if $a_1, a_2 \in A$. Does $A$ have positive density?

*References:*
- [Ben Green's Open Problem 63](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#section.8)
- [erdosproblems.com/424](https://www.erdosproblems.com/424)

This file points to the canonical formalization in `FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«424»`.
-/

findings.description: The canonical-reference claim at line 30 silently identifies different generating rules. This module only imports ErdosProblems/424, whose Erdos424.nextGeneration requires x ≠ y. Green's displayed condition, reproduced at lines 23–24, has no distinctness restriction. Consequently the imported generatedSet is not the set defined by that literal condition: 8 = 3*3-1 belongs to the unrestricted closure, whereas I proved 8 ∉ Erdos424.generatedSet in Lean without sorryAx. There is a genuine source ambiguity, however: Green also identifies his set with OEIS A005244 and Erdős #424, both of which use distinct factors. I have not established that the two density questions are inequivalent, so this is a modeling concern rather than a definitive misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 Open Problems, Problem 63, pp. 30–31 (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf): 'a₁a₂ − 1 ∈ A if a₁, a₂ ∈ A.' The following comments identify A with A005244. In contrast, https://www.erdosproblems.com/424 explicitly requires i ≠ j, and https://oeis.org/A005244 begins 2, 3, 5, 9, 14, omitting 8.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify which interpretation this forwarding module formalizes. To preserve Green's literal displayed condition, add a separate unrestricted-factor construction and question here, leaving the distinct-factor Erdős version intact. Alternatively, explicitly document that the module follows Green's OEIS/Erdős cross-reference and state the distinctness condition in the docstring. Do not silently regard the two sets as identical.

findings.description: The advertised canonical theorem Erdos424.erdos_424 uses generatedSet.HasPosDensity. Unfolding this asserts existence of a positive natural-density limit: ∃ d > 0, Tendsto (N ↦ #(generatedSet ∩ [0,N))/N) atTop (𝓝 d). The cited Erdős page instead explains the likely intended question using positive lower density, which does not require convergence. No justification that these notions coincide for generatedSet is supplied or was established during this review. This is debatable rather than a definite error because Green says only 'positive density' and the Erdős page qualifies its lower-density interpretation with 'most likely'.
findings.source_evidence: The commentary at https://www.erdosproblems.com/424 says: 'by positive density he most likely meant positive lower density' and explicitly asks whether there exists c > 0 such that, for all large x, the number of sequence values in [1,x] is at least cx. Green's Problem 63 uses the unqualified phrase 'positive density'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the density convention explicit. For the lower-density interpretation, use answer(sorry) ↔ 0 < Erdos424.generatedSet.lowerDensity, or the equivalent eventual counting lower bound. If retaining the natural-density question, label it as that interpretation or as a separate stronger variant instead of treating the conventions as interchangeable.

reformulations.difference: For the distinct-factor interpretation in Erdős #424, the canonical import uses the union of simultaneous finite generations rather than describing a sequence formed by appending new values.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The stages are increasing. If two distinct elements occur at stages m and n, both occur at stage max(m,n), so their product minus one occurs at the next stage. Conversely, induction shows that every set containing 2 and 3 and closed under the distinct-factor operation contains every stage. Thus generatedSet is precisely the least such closed set and agrees with exhaustively appending generated values. The corresponding least-set iff was proved in the scratch file. This equivalence does not identify it with Green's literal unrestricted-factor closure.

could_not_verify: file: Green's unrestricted displayed rule conflicts with his distinct-factor OEIS/Erdős identification. I could not settle which convention Green intended or establish equivalence of the resulting positive-density questions.

Erdos424.erdos_424 (the canonical import): I could not establish equivalence of positive lower density and existence of a positive natural-density limit for generatedSet. The relevant page of the original Erdős 1977 reference was not accessible; the available problem-page interpretation is explicitly tentative.
review.notes: The reviewed file has no declarations or category/answer records of its own; the findings concern its unqualified canonical-reference claim. Both available problem sources still record the question as open, consistent with the imported research open tag. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully. They establish that all generated elements are at least 2, so natural-number subtraction introduces no truncation issue; verify empty/singleton generation and the density cutoff at zero; prove the least-distinct-closure characterization and the witness separating the two sets; and compute the distinct-factor sequence through 250, matching OEIS. The separating proofs have no sorryAx dependency. No definite misformalization is asserted beyond the two modeling concerns described above.
